commentary: The waterfall is under pressure from both ends. Spot rates for H100 collapsed to $0.34/hr on Vast.ai even as 1-year contracts jumped 40% to $2.35/hr (SemiAnalysis), signaling tight on-demand capacity but surplus marketplace supply. B200 on-demand ($5.66 typical) commands only 2.4× the H100 contract rate despite 2.4× VRAM, suggesting Blackwell's premium is narrowing faster than expected. Meanwhile, Amazon shortened server life to 5 years while Meta/MSFT/GOOGL stretched to 5.5-6 years on the same cohort—a $176B accounting gap Burry flags. CoreWeave's 855-bp CDS (50% default odds) and $7.5B GPU-backed debt now price the risk that depreciation schedules assumed in loan covenants exceed economic life, especially as H100 rental rates fell 70% from 2024 peaks yet remain 'fully booked' per CoreWeave disclosures—a paradox that only resolves if inference demand absorbs the cascade or if reported utilization overstates reality.
